meaning: The number 760 has no well-established or prominent symbolic meaning in biblical or Jewish tradition.
description: 760 is not a number that is highlighted specially in the Bible or in classical Jewish numerology (gematria) with a generally recognized symbolic interpretation. The number appears in the Bible in connection with censuses and genealogies, among other things as the number of descendants of Zakkai who returned from exile in Babylon. Although gematria can link Hebrew words to the number 760, there is no broad consensus on a special symbolic meaning. Some may point to historical events, such as that 760 BC falls within the time of the prophets in Israel, but this does not give the number its own symbolic status in tradition.

footnotes.text: The number 760 appears in Ezra 2:9 and Nehemiah 7:14 as the count of descendants of Zakkai (also written Sakkai) who returned from the Babylonian exile. In 1 Chronicles 5:18, 44,760 men fit for battle are mentioned from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh.
